idiom_name: opaque repo struct + typed accessor functions with prepared SQLite statements
implementation_notes: C has no classes, no persistence framework and no collection vocabulary beyond arrays, so the repository is a hand-written module: an opaque struct owns the connection and a set of typed accessor functions is the collection interface. The SQLite C API supplies the primitives - sqlite3_open_v2/sqlite3_prepare_v2/sqlite3_bind_*/sqlite3_step/sqlite3_column_* - and the row-to-struct copy is written by hand (C has no mapper). When the store must be swappable, emulate the interface with a struct of function pointers; otherwise a single module with static SQL is the honest form.
pitfalls: Every path - including error returns - must call sqlite3_finalize; a leaked statement keeps a read lock on the database and leaks memory, and C has no RAII to save you.
A sqlite3* handle and its statements are not thread-safe in the default threading mode: share one handle per thread, or open with SQLITE_OPEN_FULLMUTEX and serialise at the repository boundary.
Query results are arrays the caller must free: state the ownership rule in the interface (caller-provided buffer or an explicit invoice_list_free) or every caller invents a different leak.
